newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Burns Philp settles Estate Mortgage.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Burns Philp settles Estate Mortgage.

text.p: Spices and yeast group Burns Philp & Co Ltd said on Monday it had settled its long-running Estate Mortgage legal dispute with Meridian Investment Trust .
Burns Philp said the settlement was for A$90 million in cash and 12 million convertible notes at A$2.20 each.
"Burns Philp and the trustees will request that legal proceedings be adjourned pending satisfaction of the conditions precedent," Burns Philp said.

"The settlement includes a cash payment of A$90 million and the issue of 12 million convertible notes at an issue price of $A2.20 per note having a five-year duration and convertible on a one-for-one basis at any time during the term of the notes."

The notes will have a coupon rate of six percent per annum with interest payable quarterly. "This settlement will meet all claims against the company arising out of the administration of the Estate Mortgage Trusts," Burns Philp said.
Burns Philp Chairman Alan McGregor said he was pleased all claims against the company had been settled as it would allow the company to concentrate fully on its current businesses.

"Estate Mortgage has taken up many hours of management time and the costs associated with mounting a complex legal case such as this are significant," McGregor said. "The company is pleased to have this issue behind it," he said.

"Our key ongoing priorities are to successfully sell our North American and European herb and spice businesses and to pursue the numerous growth opportunities available to the company in our global yeast businesses," he said.

Burns Philp's Burns Philp Trustee Co was the trustee for investment group Estate Mortgage Trusts between 1983 and 1990 when the group collapsed, losing over A$600 million invested by 56,000 mostly elderly unit holders.
Meridian settled with Estate Mortgage's auditors Priestley & Morris in April, receiving a A$31 million payout in an out-of-court settlement.
Meridian said the Burns Philp settlement would deliver to the trusts a minimum value of A$116.4 million.

The settlement was conditional on judicial advice affirming the trustees were justified in settling and approval from unitholders. Meridian trustee John Murphy said the settlement was pleasing. He said the settlement applied only to the litigation between the trustees and Burns Philp.

"The litigation against the remaining defendants, including Freehill Hollingdale & Page, Burns Philp Trustee Company and various former directors of Burns Philp Trustee, will continue, as will the separate case against Burns Philp Trustee's professional indemnity insurers," Murphy said.
"We will continue to pursue the remaining defendants vigorously," he said.
Murphy told Reuters that Burns Philp Trustee Co was however no longer of concequence and did not tie the parent Burns Philp into the legal action any longer.
Tyndall Australia Ltd, which manages Meridian, said the settlement would substantially strengthen the trust's financial position.
An information memorandum detailing how the funds would be distributed would be sent to the unitholders within the next month, it said.
"Unitholders, will then have the opportunity to consider the proposed settlement in a general meeting in early September," Tyndall Managing Director Michael Wilkins said in a statement.
Burns Philps' shares were up five cents at A$2.49 by 10.50 a.m. (0050 GMT). Meridian's shares were up 13 cents at A$1.60.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
